problems.source_says: Elaboration is a deterministic count of words remaining after NLTK stopword removal. The supplied codebook defines automated_score as a creativity scoring model (semantic-distance scoring or a language model judge); automatic computation alone does not meet that definition. The form explicitly broadens this category to an automated word count without codebook support. No listed measure code explicitly covers plain word count, so measure should remain null with the word-count procedure preserved in measure_detail unless the codebook is expanded. The elaboration construct and output unit are supported.
problems.quote: We computed the elaboration score of each idea by counting the number of words after removal of the stopwords using NLTK (Bird et al., 2009) and the stop words corpus provided with it.
problems.locator: PDF p. 7, Participants Elaboration, first paragraph and equation (3); creativity-codebook.md, section 6, Measure table (automated_score).

confirmed.statement: Criterion 3 holds: two independent human raters scored the originality of submitted ideas on a seven-point scale, and OCSAI also scored originality. These are evaluations of creative output, not participant self-reports.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 5, Data collection; p. 7, Ideas’ Originality, first two paragraphs.

confirmed.statement: S1-O1 and S1-O4 measure novelty: the originality prompt asks whether an idea breaks away from conventional or existing solutions. It does not measure diversity across people.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 7, Ideas’ Originality, originality-rating prompt; creativity-codebook.md, section 6, Construct table.

confirmed.statement: For S1-O1, S1-O2, and S1-O3, AI was available during output production in the AI arms: the peer supplied two ideas per round or one idea per three user submissions in live collaboration. Their with_ai classification and immediate timing are supported.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 4, Intervention Design; p. 5, Workshop Session; creativity-codebook.md, section 1, question-assignment rule.

confirmed.statement: S1-O2 is fluency measured by counting each participant’s ideas and normalizing to 15 minutes using the group’s activity duration; category_count and participant are supported.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 6, Participant’s Creative Fluency; p. 7, equation (1) and accompanying text; creativity-codebook.md, section 6.

confirmed.statement: S1-O3 measures elaboration through the length of each idea after stopword removal; elaboration and output are correct despite the measure-code issue.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 7, Participants Elaboration, first paragraph and equation (3); creativity-codebook.md, section 6.

confirmed.statement: The paper explicitly analyzes fluency at participant level and elaboration and originality at idea level, without group-level or multilevel modeling. The recorded analysis units are correct.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 6, analysis-level paragraph; p. 14, Limitations, first paragraph.

confirmed.statement: S1-O1 and S1-O4 appropriately leave measure null: human ratings and OCSAI are documented, but the reported originality effects and author comparison do not identify which score was used. Figure 4 labels its axis only Originality (normalized).
confirmed.locator: PDF pp. 7-8, Ideas’ Originality and equation (4); p. 8, Figures 3-4, inspected in memory; p. 13, Using GLMs to Automatically Assess Idea Originality.

confirmed.statement: S1-O1 matches the printed effects: live d = -0.17, 94% HDI [-0.44, 0.10]; rounds d = -0.24, 94% HDI [-0.51, 0.01]. Both intervals include zero, supporting no_clear_difference.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 8, Ideas’ Originality, paragraph following equation (4).

confirmed.statement: S1-O2 matches all four effects: AI versus no AI, live -0.61 [-1.22, -0.07] and rounds 0.16 [-0.37, 0.67]; rounds versus live, with AI -0.04 [-0.52, 0.45] and without AI -0.79 [-1.39, -0.26]. All intervals are 94% HDIs.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 7, Participant’s Creative Fluency, paragraph following equation (2); p. 6, Figure 1.

confirmed.statement: S1-O3 matches the printed effects: live d = 0.05, 94% HDI [-0.19, 0.3]; rounds d = -0.01, 94% HDI [-0.26, 0.26].
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 7, Participants Elaboration, paragraph following equation (3).

confirmed.statement: S1-O4 matches the author-group summaries: AI mean 0.64, median 0.64, SD 0.12, N = 156; human mean 0.44, median 0.44, SD 0.16, N = 426. The one-sided Mann-Whitney result is U = 56620, p < .001.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 8, Ideas’ Originality, paragraph preceding equation (4).

confirmed.statement: S1-O4 correctly transcribes the Shapiro-Wilk results: AI W = 0.98, p = .014; human W = 0.99, p = 0.001.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 8, Ideas’ Originality, paragraph preceding equation (4).

confirmed.statement: The additional originality correlations are correct: human raters r = .45; rater 1 versus OCSAI r = .57; rater 2 versus OCSAI r = .62; mean human rating versus OCSAI r = .70; all p < .001.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 7, final paragraph; p. 8, opening paragraph and Figure 3.

confirmed.statement: The ancillary duration correlations in S1-O2 match: rounds N = 10, r(8) = 0.94, p < 0.001; live N = 9, r(7) = -0.65, p = 0.059. These Ns count groups.

The retained pool contains 582 ideas, comprising 156 AI and 426 human ideas. These support the recorded pool counts; the paper does not separately print an observation denominator for the human-condition originality model.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 6, relevance-filtering paragraph; p. 8, author-group summaries and equation (4).

confirmed.statement: S1-O4 is an output-level comparison by idea author using the same experimental pool, rather than an estimate of giving people AI assistance. Its contextual question none and mixed availability preserve that distinction.
confirmed.locator: PDF pp. 4-5, experimental conditions and data collection; p. 8, author-group comparison; creativity-codebook.md, sections 1 and 3, AI-versus-human context evidence.

confirmed.statement: No additional outcome answering the three atlas questions was found: relevance scores serve filtering; co-construction compares collaboration modalities; UEQ-S and qualitative responses concern experience. No scored across-person similarity or unassisted post-AI task is reported.
confirmed.locator: Complete markdown conversion, lines 1-495, including references; PDF pp. 6-7, relevance filtering; pp. 8-9, Collaboration Between Participants; pp. 9-13, User Experience and discussion; pp. 14-17, conclusion and references. No appendix is present.

summary: Eligibility holds because participants’ ideas were rated and counted, and the reported numbers match the PDF. Elaboration’s word count is incorrectly coded as automated_score under the supplied codebook.
